question: What is the visual style and emotional tone of Spider-Man: Brand New Day's poster?
Which titles have a dark, tense poster tone?
What is Dhurandhar's poster composition style?
Which titles have vibrant, uplifting posters?
List all titles with character-focused poster composition
Show me the poster for Dhurandhar
Which titles have a warm dominant color tone?
How many titles have been tagged with poster signals so far?
Which titles have minimalist poster composition?
What is the visual style and emotional tone of a title's poster?
sql:
SELECT t.title_name, p.dominant_color_tone, p.composition_style, p.emotional_tone
FROM dataflix.content_signals.poster_signals p
JOIN dataflix.core.dim_title t ON p.title_id = t.title_id
WHERE t.title_name ILIKE '%Spider-Man: Brand New Day%'

question: Which titles have a given poster tone or style?
sql:
SELECT t.title_name, p.dominant_color_tone, p.composition_style, p.emotional_tone
FROM dataflix.content_signals.poster_signals p
JOIN dataflix.core.dim_title t ON p.title_id = t.title_id
WHERE p.emotional_tone = 'tense'

question: Show me the poster for a title
sql:
SELECT t.title_name, p.poster_url
FROM dataflix.content_signals.poster_signals p
JOIN dataflix.core.dim_title t ON p.title_id = t.title_id
WHERE t.title_name ILIKE '%Dhurandhar%'

content:
This space covers real poster-art tagging: dominant_color_tone, composition_style, and emotional_tone. These tags come from a real vision-FM model (databricks-llama-4-maverick) analyzing the actual real TMDB poster image for each title -- not fabricated or templated, though each field is constrained to a fixed controlled vocabulary rather than free text.
dominant_color_tone is one of: warm, cool, neutral, high-contrast, muted, dark, vibrant.
composition_style is one of: character-focused, ensemble, action-collage, minimalist, text-heavy, landscape/establishing.
emotional_tone is one of: tense, uplifting, dark, comedic, dramatic, mysterious, romantic.
Coverage is intentionally PARTIAL -- only a 20-title subset (the top 15 Hollywood + top 5 Bollywood titles by real TMDB vote_count) has been tagged, not the full 130-title catalog. If a title isn't in poster_signals, say tagging data isn't available for it rather than implying no poster exists.
There is no dialogue-pacing or subtitle data in this space or anywhere in Dataflix -- if asked about pacing or dialogue density, say that signal isn't available. Thumbnail-VARIANT-performance data DOES exist (see the 'marketing' Genie Space) -- don't say it's unavailable.
TITLE MATCHING RULE: always match title_name with ILIKE '%<name>%' (case-insensitive, partial), never exact '='. The user's phrasing may have typos or be a partial name -- if a fuzzy match returns more than one title, show all matches rather than guessing. If ILIKE finds NO match at all, the name may be misspelled (not just partial) -- fall back to levenshtein(lower(title_name), lower('<name_as_given>')) ORDER BY that value ASC LIMIT 3, and treat a result with distance <= 5 as the likely intended title (e.g. levenshtein('durandhar the revenge', 'dhurandhar: the revenge') = 1). State in your answer that you matched a likely misspelling, e.g. "(matched 'Durandhar the Revenge' to 'Dhurandhar: The Revenge')", rather than silently substituting it.
title_id format is '{movie|tv}_{tmdb_id}' -- always join to dim_title to resolve title_name rather than showing raw title_id.
Both hero titles are tagged: 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' (movie_969681) and 'Dhurandhar' (movie_1291608).
poster_url is a real, live, publicly-accessible TMDB image CDN URL for the title's actual UNMODIFIED poster (not a placeholder, and not one of the derived thumbnail variants from the 'marketing' space -- always label it 'Original' so it's never confused with a variant). ANY question that relates to a title's poster, thumbnail, or visual/artwork appearance in any way (not just an explicit 'show me') -- including questions about dominant_color_tone, composition_style, or emotional_tone -- MUST include the poster_url value verbatim as part of the answer, formatted as: '**Original poster:**\n\n![<title_name> - Original](<poster_url>)'. Do not just describe the URL in words or omit it -- output the actual markdown image tag so it can render, with the blank-line spacing shown.
Formatting rule for the image markdown: it MUST be its own paragraph, with a full BLANK LINE (two newlines) before it and, if any text follows, a full blank line after it too. NEVER put the image tag on the line immediately after a label or heading with only a single newline -- a single newline is not a paragraph break and will visually merge the label and image together. Correct example:

**Poster:**

![Dhurandhar poster](https://image.tmdb.org/t/p/w500/xyz.jpg)

Incorrect (do not do this): '**Poster:**\n![Dhurandhar poster](url)' with only one newline.
VOCABULARY MAPPING RULE: dominant_color_tone, composition_style, and emotional_tone are each constrained to the fixed vocabularies listed above -- a user will often describe a poster using a word NOT in that vocabulary (e.g. 'gritty', 'bright', 'scary', 'epic'). Never filter directly on the user's literal word if it isn't one of the allowed values -- map it to the nearest semantic match instead (e.g. 'gritty'->'dark', 'bright'->'vibrant', 'scary'->'tense', 'epic'->'ensemble' or 'dramatic' depending on context) and state in the answer which controlled value you used, e.g. "(interpreting 'gritty' as the 'dark' tone)".
